title: MidPul respiratory physiology fragment Q34-40
note: Two preferred photos forwarded from a 2024-07-21 post. Only source Q34-40 are supplied; Q1-33 are not fabricated. Yellow highlights are unofficial selections. Source numbering and option order retained.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the volume of air that remains in the lungs at the end of a normal expiration?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The volume remaining after normal expiration is FRC = ERV + RV.

questions.prompt: Which of following statement is not true about pulmonary surfactant?
options: Helps to empty small alveoli to larger alveoli.
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Surfactant stabilizes small alveoli by lowering their surface tension; it prevents rather than promotes their emptying into larger alveoli.

questions.prompt: Which of the following air ducts is able to exchange respiratory gases between lung and blood?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Respiratory bronchioles have alveoli interrupting their walls and begin the gas-exchange zone. The third option is printed only as Respiratory; bronchiole is inferred from the preceding non-respiratory bronchiole distractor, not added to the transcription.

questions.prompt: The FEV1/FVC is less than 80% at.....
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: B is the intended obstructive-pattern answer: obstruction lowers the ratio. The source's universal 80% cutoff is oversimplified; assessment uses age-appropriate lower limits and clinical context. Source image visually reads 80%, not the OCR's 50%.

questions.prompt: The O2 - Hb dissociation curve is shifted to left by.....
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Increased pH raises hemoglobin's oxygen affinity and shifts the curve left.

questions.prompt: Which of the following causes vasoconstriction of the pulmonary arteries?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Reduced local alveolar PO2 is the key signal for hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction in this comparison.

questions.prompt: Which of following can be measured by spirometer?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Inspiratory capacity does not include residual volume and can be measured by simple spirometry; RV, FRC and TLC cannot.

excludedItems.reason: The start of the original paper (Q1-33) is absent from this two-image fragment, not silently reconstructed.

audit.notes: All preferred source images visually reviewed; OCR used only as a drafting aid. All supplied complete items retained. Source annotations are unofficial, preserved separately from the audited answer. Null audited keys deliberately quarantine ambiguous or defective questions. Numbered options 1-4 and Persian letters are normalized to A-D in displayed order.
